newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks slip as Wall St falls, dlr firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks slip as Wall St falls, dlr firm.

text.p: Leading European stock markets turned lower on Friday, weighed down in part by Wall Street, but the dollar was buoyant after a one-yen climb overnight.
Dealers had expected some European markets to open strongly, notably Paris and Frankfurt which closed at record highs on Thursday.
But the dead hand of Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.46 percent on Thursday, helped to pull most European share prices lower in mid-morning trade.
However, losses on the main continental markets were slight and dealers said prices were generally consolidating after record runs and sentiment remained buoyant.
Wall Street worries about company earnings and rising long-term interest rates before Federal Reserve policy-makers meet next Tuesday and Wednesday dragged the Dow down 35.73 points to 7,654.25.
London, which has worries of its own, was down 0.64 percent on Friday, Paris blue chips dropped 0.21 percent and Frankfurt gave up early modest gains to fall just 0.02 percent.

In London, the FTSE-100 index fell 29.8 points to 4,628.1 as dealers worried about a report suggesting that finance minister Gordon Brown would impose a hefty five billion pound ($8 billion) windfall tax on utilities in next Wednesday's budget.
The Financial Times also reported he wanted to push ahead with the abolition of a corporate tax break on dividends despite pressure from the financial community.
Labour was elected in May with a promise to impose the windfall tax but the market has swung on speculation on how big it would be and which utilities would be hit most.
By midmorning shares in British Telecom, which is seen paying out up to one billion pounds, were down 8.5 pence at 447.

Other targets are expected to be regional electricity companies, the two main generators, the water companies, companies spun out of British Gas, railway infrastucture operator Railtrack and airport operator BAA, the FT said.
In Paris prices opened higher but the CAC-40 index of blue chips then slipped 6.18 points to 2,887.46.
One broker said investors were normally more cautious before the weekend and the market needed a small correction after hitting successive highs this week which took the CAC to 2,900.
Rhone-Poulenc fell 2.3 percent to 246.7 francs on profit taking after rising almost 20 percent on Thursday due to the possibility it will buy out its U.S. unit Rorer.

In Germany the DAX index also lost an early gain and was down just 0.6 of a point at 3,804.69. But car-makers were firm after failing to keep up with the recent overall market rally. Volkswagen gained 23 marks to 1,300.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was above 114 yen after the one-yen climb overnight. This was due to gloomy output forecasts for Japan and rising unemployment which dampened rate-hike expectations.
Japan produced a large amount of economic data, including retail sales, industrial production and unemployment, as European market were opening.

The dollar initially dropped after release of industrial output figures but it quickly gained momentum as the market focused on forward-looking data issued by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).

These forecasts showed a decrease of 2.6 percent in June and an increase of just 0.9 percent in July. Analysts also said comments by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita, had also weighed on the yen.
Matsushita said that if the official discount rate were raised prematurely it would negatively affect the economy.

"The industrial production numbers were strong, but the market chose to focus on the output forecasts for June and July, which were a fair bit weaker, and the jobless rate," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN AMRO
"They served to allay market fears of an imminent tightening in policy."

By mid morning the dollar stood at 114.14 yen against 113.22 yen in late Europe on Thursday, just off the high of 114.27 hit earlier in Europe. It was was steady against the mark, trading at 1.7264 against 1.7265.

The dollar mostly ignored an admission by French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn after Thursday's close that Paris could not cut its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year, a key target for joining the single European currency.

But with speculation growing that the targets will be interpreted liberally, Strauss-Kahn said Paris was committed to joining the single currency on time in 1999 and said he had no intention of letting the deficit run out of control.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 114.14 yen and 1.7264 marks in late Europe, compared with 113.22 yen and 1.7265 marks in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index down 29.8 points at 4,628.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 slipped 6.18 points to 2,887.46.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down just 0.6 of a point at 3,804.69.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was $337.40 an ounce against $338.15 at Thursday's close. Silver was at $4.75.
